title: Shooting stuns friend
article: A 40-year-old Chemainus man was shot by a North Cowichan/Duncan RCMP officer during a traffic stop after he put his lighter in his pocket and raised his hands, says the passenger in the vehicle.

Dale Brewer, 40, also of Chemainus, said that his friend, Bill Gillespie, who was driving the car, didn't have any weapons and didn't threaten the officer when they were pulled over on Friday night and ordered out of their car by officers with guns drawn.
Gillespie was shot in the upper body; he is now at Royal Jubilee Hospital in critical condition.

In an interview with the Times Colonist, Brewer said he and Gillespie were driving home from an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting around 9:20 p.m. and were approaching Brewer's house on Henry Road when a charcoal-coloured police SUV sounded its siren. They drove two blocks to 3020 Henry Rd. and pulled into the driveway.
Brewer said they didn't stop immediately because Gillespie was scared, nervous and only two blocks from the home.

Two plainclothes officers with bulletproof vests and guns raised yelled at the men to get out of the car, put their hands up and get on their knees, Brewer said. They got out of the four-door brown Saturn, Brewer said, but Gillespie put his lighter into his pocket, an action that might have been a tragic mistake.

"Next thing I know, he got shot and I was getting cuffed on the ground. And all I could see was Bill's face full of blood," he said. "In my eyes, from what I seen, there was no reason for them to shoot him."
He said Gillespie, who was about three metres away from the officer, wasn't yelling or being aggressive. He suggested the officer could have used a Taser or pepper spray instead.

Brewer also claims the officers didn't have a first-aid kit to treat Gillespie, who was bleeding and convulsing. He said Gillespie didn't receive medical attention until an ambulance arrived 10 minutes later.

RCMP have released few details about the incident. Yesterday, they wouldn't say why the two men were stopped, why the officer fired or if he had a Taser available to him, and wouldn't confirm or deny what Brewer said.

The Vancouver Island Integrated Major Crime Unit has been called in to investigate the shooting and was on scene yesterday. An observer with the Commission for Public Complaints Against the RCMP is also monitoring the probe.
Cpl. Darren Lagan, Island district RCMP spokesman, said major crime investigators have interviewed the officers, who have four-and-a-half and five years' experience with the detachment.

Lagan stressed that the two men pulled over are well-known to police. Court records show in November 2006, Gillespie was sentenced to 16 months in jail and three years' probation for a March 2005 robbery, in which he was in possession of a firearm.
Lagan said police take extra precautions when dealing with individuals with criminal records.

"I'm speaking generally -- if I pull somebody over and I know that individual, I know that individual has a history of violence or that individual has a history involving weapons, then obviously my sense in processing that environment has changed," Lagan said.
He added that vehicle stops can be very dangerous for officers because they don't always know who is in the vehicle.
However, Brewer said he can't think of why they were pulled over; Gillespie was not speeding and had no drugs in the car, he said. "I've never been pulled over with a cop having their gun on me."
Brewer said he was arrested, taken to the police station, and told he could be charged for evading police. At 6 a.m. Saturday, he was released without charge after giving a statement.
Brewer said he and Gillespie have fought drug addictions and were trying to get clean.

The last time the North Cowichan/Duncan RCMP detachment shot a man was March 1, when a senior officer fired at a man coming at him with a knife in his trailer in the Duncan RV Park. Derek Welton, 39, was pronounced dead in hospital later that night. A coroner's inquest will take place in that case.
